chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Ali ibn Uqba, from Al-Husayn ibn Musa, from Bureyd and Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The one who buys the food of a people while they are reluctant to sell it to him, his flesh will be clipped for them on the Day of Resurrection.
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual consequence of buying food from people who do not want to sell it?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to illustrate the spiritual consequences of coercive trade (gharar and ikrah), emphasizing that violating the seller's free will incurs a literal recompense. This physical clipping of flesh serves as a vivid metaphor for the buyer consuming the seller's essence or vitality unjustly, a concept deeply rooted in Shia jurisprudence regarding valid contracts. The hadith underscores that consent is not merely a legal formality but a spiritual condition for the validity of the exchange in the sight of God.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Hassan Bin Ali, from Ali Bin Uqba, from Al Husayn Bin Musa, from Bureyd and Muhammad Bin Muslim, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The one who buys the food of a people and they are compelled to it (dislike to sell it), it would be clipped for them from his flesh on the Day of Judgement’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Hassan ibn Ali from Ali ibn ‘Uqbah from al-Husayn ibn Musa from Burayd and Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
If one buys the foodstuff of a people who dislike such purchase, on the Day of Judgment it will be recovered for them from his flesh.’”
